title: One digest rotation: publish every pending command kind on the shared runtime contract at once
description:
THE SHARED CONTRACT LEAF. Filed by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-06 in answer to the governor's #architects request of 20:07, after the THIRD collision in one day on the same two digest mirrors (task-40e52fa8 14:15, task-c2b5a9f0 rescue 19:39, task-06ac0da1 reopened tonight).

THE PROBLEM THIS ROW ENDS. Adding ANY kind to RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS rotates GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST by construction - contract-digest.ts puts `commandKinds: sortedCopy(RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS)` inside canonicalContractSurface(), which deriveContractDigest() SHA256s. Every publishing row therefore edits THE SAME SIX FILES and invalidates every sibling's digest the moment it lands. FOUR rows are queued to do exactly that tonight, each with its own plan, each touching the same six paths:
- task-37a50989 `deployment.rollback`
- task-5a8c3166 `deployment.migrate_down`
- task-bb0a7131 `project.set_agent_provider`
- task-06ac0da1 `design.submit` and `design.read`
They cannot run concurrently and they serialise badly: whoever lands second re-does the census, the regeneration and the four mirrors against a digest the first one moved. All four are WORKING with NO assignee, so nothing is mid-flight and this can be fixed properly rather than worked around.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: ONE roster edit adding ALL FIVE remaining strings, ONE regeneration, ONE mirror census, ONE digest rotation. Six files, once.

THE FIVE STRINGS, in sorted position: `deployment.migrate_down`, `deployment.rollback`, `design.read`, `design.submit`, `project.set_agent_provider`. VERIFY EACH ONE IS STILL ABSENT before adding it - a sibling may have landed one meanwhile, and re-adding a member is invisible in a Set-based count (a duplicate SHRINKS the set rather than growing it, which is why runtime-contract.test.ts pins `commands.size` by literal and its own comment says so).

MEASURED AT HEAD 3891a2a0 (2026-09-06): the roster already carries deployment.deploy, deployment.set_target, environment.set_variable, environment.unset_variable, preview.decide, release.decide and repository.bootstrap - so the pattern is proven and this row follows a trail four rows have already cut.

THE TRAP THAT CAUSED ALL THREE COLLISIONS: two of the four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors live under apps/control-room (data-adapter.test.ts and v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx), and apps/control-room is in NONE of `pnpm test` (the root vitest include has no apps/**), `pnpm typecheck` (it is a runtime value compare) or `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. A forgotten mirror ships two HARD-THROWING tests behind three green gates. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is the only leg that sees them, and it is this row's named verification command.

AFTER THIS LANDS, every consumer row drops its contract files and keeps only its daemon work. Their dependsOn has been set to this row.

NOT IN SCOPE: any daemon vocabulary, family, registry, roster test, MCP fence or dispatch handler. Those stay with the four consumer rows.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.
definitionOfDone: All five strings - `deployment.migrate_down`, `deployment.rollback`, `design.read`, `design.submit`, `project.set_agent_provider` - are members of RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS in SORTED position, each VERIFIED ABSENT immediately before being added (a sibling may have landed one; a duplicate member SHRINKS the Set rather than growing it and is invisible to a naive count). runtime-contract.test.ts agrees in BOTH coupled assertions: the hand-transcribed EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS list and the `commands.size` literal. Do NOT derive the expected list from the tuple - that file's comment forbids it and a derived list asserts nothing. Take the size from the PRINTED expected-vs-received, never from arithmetic.

The generated client was REGENERATED, never hand-edited: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`, with the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST both quoted in the completion record. An UNCHANGED digest means the generator did not see the new kinds - a stop, not a pass. contract-digest.test.ts DERIVES the digest rather than pinning it, so it must go green WITHOUT being edited; if it needs an edit, the generate step was skipped.

THE MIRROR CENSUS IS RUN, NOT QUOTED: `git grep -n <old digest> -- . ':!.moe' ':!pnpm-lock.yaml'` BEFORE the change (expect exactly four hits) and AFTER (expect zero), across ALL file types - a `--include=*.ts` grep misses the .tsx mirror, which is one of the two that caused three collisions today. Every hit carries the new hex, including GENERATED_FILE_SHA256 beside CONTRACT_DIGEST in generated-coverage.test.ts. A FIFTH hit is a stop-and-report.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line: revert ONLY apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx to the old digest and confirm `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` goes RED with the compat gate's own refusal message. That drill is this row's most valuable artifact - it is the only proof the two apps/control-room mirrors are covered by any gate at all, and its absence is what let three rows ship past them.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (MANDATORY), `pnpm typecheck`, and root `pnpm test` - stating plainly that the root lane covers NO apps/** file.

The diff touches EXACTLY six files and ZERO under apps/daemon/: runtime-vocabulary.ts, runtime-contract.test.ts, generated-client.ts, generated-coverage.test.ts, data-adapter.test.ts, approve-plan.test.tsx. Prove it with `git status --porcelain -- apps/ packages/` in the completion record. A daemon file here means a consumer row's work leaked into the leaf.
taskRails: CONTRACT SURFACE ONLY, AND ALL OF IT AT ONCE. This row exists so the digest rotates exactly once for five kinds instead of five times for one each. It wires no daemon command, defines no refusal code, fences no principal and serves no query.
NEVER hand-edit the generated client. It is generator output; the only legal way to change it is `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`.

CENSUS THE MIRRORS WITH A FULL-TREE `git grep` OF THE LITERAL, across all file types. The set has moved twice and a *.ts-only grep misses the .tsx one - that exact miss caused three collisions on 2026-09-05.
`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` IS MANDATORY: two mirrors live there and no other gate sees them.
VERIFY EACH STRING IS ABSENT BEFORE ADDING IT. A duplicate member shrinks the Set and hides in every count.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE AND BASELINE. NO EDITS. This row is the choke point for eight consumer rows, so measure rather than trust anything below. (a) VERIFY EACH OF THE FIVE STRINGS IS STILL ABSENT, individually: `for k in deployment.migrate_down deployment.rollback design.read design.submit project.set_agent_provider; do grep -c "\"$k\"" packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts; done` — all five returned 0 at plan time (HEAD 3891a2a0). A string that is now PRESENT means a sibling landed it despite the dependsOn rewire: DROP IT from your edit rather than adding it twice, because `commands.size` is a SET size and a duplicate member SHRINKS it, which passes no test and is invisible in every count. The file's own comment at :107 says exactly that. (b) RECORD THE OLD DIGEST AND CENSUS THE MIRRORS, full tree, ALL FILE TYPES — the `--include=*.ts` habit is precisely what missed the `.tsx` mirror three times yesterday: read the literal from `generated-client.ts:919`, then `git grep -n <hex> -- . ':!.moe' ':!pnpm-lock.yaml'`. At plan time the digest was `f07b77e49025d5fd8a6bd391f5848f24103390d23e4db11523346b87f0891bfd` and there were EXACTLY FOUR hits: generated-client.ts:919 (source of truth), generated-coverage.test.ts:36 (CONTRACT_DIGEST, beside GENERATED_FILE_SHA256 at :35 = 9a4bed62…), apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18, apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255. A FIFTH hit is a stop-and-report. (c) READ THE TWO COUPLED ASSERTIONS AND NOTE THE ONE THAT IS ORDER-SENSITIVE: runtime-contract.test.ts:106 is `expect(RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS).toEqual(EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS)` — a `toEqual` between ARRAYS, so the hand-transcribed list must match the tuple in ORDER, not merely as a set. Line 108 pins `commands.size` at 110 (a literal, and its comment explains why it is not `.length`). Both move. The list is documented at :28-34 as hand-transcribed ON PURPOSE, so an expectation computed from the tuple can never fail — do NOT derive it. (d) BASELINE, standalone foreground, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (the slow one, ~147 files — run it now so the after-run has something to compare against), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`. Any red here is FOREIGN; quote it so step 5 can subtract it. (e) `git status --porcelain -- apps/ packages/` and note peer dirt; never revert it.

THE ROSTER EDIT — FIVE STRINGS, IN SORTED POSITION, IN TWO FILES THAT MUST AGREE IN ORDER. (1) `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts`, RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS. The measured insert points, all verified at plan time: `deployment.migrate_down` and `deployment.rollback` go on line 91 between `"deployment.deploy"` and `"deployment.set_target"` (deploy < migrate_down < rollback < set_target); `design.read` and `design.submit` follow `"deployment.set_target"` and precede `"effect.activate"` on the same line; `project.set_agent_provider` goes on line 107 after `"project.register"` and before `"provider.probe"` on line 108 (register < set_agent_provider, and project.* precedes provider.*). Add NO `satisfies RuntimeCommandKind` annotation to any member — `RuntimeCommandKind` is DERIVED from this tuple, so annotating a member is circular; the file documents that above FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_COMMAND_KIND. (2) `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts`: make THE SAME FIVE INSERTS in EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS at :35, IN THE SAME ORDER — :106's `toEqual` compares arrays, so a set-correct but order-wrong list fails with a diff that looks like a missing member. Then change the `commands.size` literal at :108 from 110 to the printed value (115 if all five are new and none was pre-landed). TAKE THAT NUMBER FROM THE PRINTED EXPECTED-VS-RECEIVED of a failing run, never from arithmetic here — if a sibling landed one of the five between this plan and your edit, the answer is not 115 and the arithmetic silently lies.

REGENERATE, THEN ROTATE ALL FOUR MIRRORS. (1) Run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` (package.json:18 = `node --experimental-strip-types generator/generate.ts`). NEVER hand-edit generated-client.ts. EXPECT A DIFF LARGER THAN ONE LINE and do not trim it: generated-coverage.test.ts pins `GENERATED_COMMAND_KINDS === LIVE_COMMAND_KINDS` and indexes `GENERATED_COMMAND_BUILDERS[kind]` for every RuntimeCommandKind, so the generator emits a builder entry per new kind as well as the rotated digest. Review the diff — that review is the whole point of committing generator output. (2) IF THE DIGEST AT :919 IS UNCHANGED, STOP. The generator did not see the new kinds, and a stale digest passes every grep while failing the compat check at runtime. (3) Rotate the three consumer mirrors to the NEW hex: `generated-coverage.test.ts:36` CONTRACT_DIGEST **and :35 GENERATED_FILE_SHA256 to the regenerated file's own sha256** — that file's header spells out this exact ritual (regenerate, review the diff, update both constants), and updating only one leaves it red; `apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18`; `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255`. (4) DO NOT EDIT `contract-pins.ts` (a bare re-export) or `contract-digest.test.ts` (it DERIVES the digest rather than pinning it, so it must go green WITHOUT an edit — if it seems to need one, the regeneration was skipped or partial). (5) Re-run the step-1 census with the OLD hex and expect ZERO hits; quote OLD and NEW in the step note.

THE DRILL THAT IS THIS ROW'S REASON FOR EXISTING. Three collisions in one day happened because two mirrors live where no ordinary gate looks; this drill is the only artifact that proves they are covered at all. `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths FIRST — all six files here are TRACKED and this row creates none, so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is the correct restore proof for each, in a call SEPARATE from the restore. State that explicitly, and state that global rail 13's untracked/SHA256 clause does NOT apply, rather than performing a ritual that proves nothing on a tracked path. THE DRILL: revert ONLY `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255` to the OLD digest, run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, and confirm it goes RED with the compat gate's own refusal message. Quote the failing line verbatim. Then restore and prove it. A SECOND DRILL worth its minute: revert only `data-adapter.test.ts:18` and confirm that mirror is independently covered too — two mirrors, two arms, because one passing does not prove the other is watched. THEN THE ARM THAT MATTERS FOR THE NEXT ROW: confirm that `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck` and root `pnpm test` ALL STAY GREEN while a mirror is reverted. That is the fact worth recording — it is why three rows shipped past these mirrors, and stating it with evidence is more useful to the next architect than any assertion in this plan.

GATES AND SELF-REVIEW. (a) GATES — standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with NO count line RAN NOTHING and is not evidence: `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (MANDATORY — the ONLY leg that sees mirrors 3 and 4), `pnpm typecheck`, and root `pnpm test` (real evidence here, because packages/contracts and packages/control-room-client are inside vitest.config.ts's include — but state plainly that it covers NO apps/** file, which is the whole trap). Attribute any red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's six owned paths; that intersection must be EMPTY. Named complete_task verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`. (b) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: is each of the five members in genuinely SORTED position in the tuple (the generator SORTS its own copy, which HIDES a source-order defect — check the tuple by eye, not the generated output); does EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS match the tuple in ORDER as well as content (:106 is an array `toEqual`); did `commands.size` move by exactly the number of strings you actually added; did a sibling land one of the five mid-flight (re-read the tuple immediately before the final gate); is `contract-digest.test.ts` green WITHOUT an edit; does `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/` show ZERO files. (c) COMPLETION RECORD — and write it for the eight rows waiting on this one, not for a grader: the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST; the four mirror paths rotated, with the before/after census counts (four, then zero); which of the five strings you actually added and which were already present; the final `commands.size`; both drill reds verbatim; and THE FACT THE NEXT ARCHITECT NEEDS — that `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck` and root `pnpm test` all stayed GREEN with a mirror reverted, which is why `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is mandatory for any row that touches this roster. Name the four consumer rows (task-06ac0da1, task-37a50989, task-5a8c3166, task-bb0a7131) so whoever claims them next knows the contract half is done and their plans' contract steps are to be dropped.

comments.content:
MEASURED AT PLAN TIME — everything a worker needs, so nothing here is re-derived. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-06, HEAD 3891a2a0. Plan approved: 5 steps, 6 files.

**All five strings confirmed absent**, checked individually: `deployment.migrate_down`, `deployment.rollback`, `design.read`, `design.submit`, `project.set_agent_provider` — `grep -c` = 0 for every one.

## The digest and its four mirrors

```
f07b77e49025d5fd8a6bd391f5848f24103390d23e4db11523346b87f0891bfd

generated-client.ts:919              GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST   (source of truth)
generated-coverage.test.ts:36        CONTRACT_DIGEST
  ... and :35                        GENERATED_FILE_SHA256 = 9a4bed62…  (same ritual, both move)
apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18
apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255
```

Full-tree grep, all file types, exactly four hits. A `--include=*.ts` census misses the `.tsx` one — that exact omission caused this three times yesterday.

## Two things in the contract test that are easy to get wrong

**`:106` is an ARRAY `toEqual`**, not a set comparison — `expect(RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS).toEqual(EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS)`. So the hand-transcribed list must match the tuple **in order**. A set-correct but order-wrong list fails with a diff that reads like a missing member and sends you hunting in the wrong place.

**`:108` pins `commands.size` at 110 by literal**, with the comment *"a duplicated member shrinks the set only."* That is the failure mode if a sibling lands one of the five mid-flight: adding a string that is already there makes the size come out **one short** with no obvious cause. Verify absence immediately before adding, and take the final number from the printed expected-vs-received rather than from 110 + 5.

## Sorted insert points, verified against neighbours

Line 91 is `"deployment.deploy", "deployment.set_target", "effect.activate",` — so migrate_down and rollback go between deploy and set_target, and the two design kinds between set_target and effect.activate. Line 107 is `"project.bind_repository", "project.register",` with `"provider.probe"` opening :108 — so `project.set_agent_provider` follows `project.register`.

## The drill is the row's actual deliverable

Step 4 reverts one mirror, requires `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` to go red, **and then confirms `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck` and root `pnpm test` all stay GREEN while it is stale.**

That last fact is the one worth recording. It is *why* three rows shipped past these mirrors, and stating it with evidence is more useful to the next architect than any assertion in the plan. Both mirrors get their own arm — one passing does not prove the other is watched.

## The completion record is a handoff

Eight rows wait on this one, four directly (`task-06ac0da1`, `task-37a50989`, `task-5a8c3166`, `task-bb0a7131` — all rewired to `dependsOn` this row). The record should name which strings actually landed, the final `commands.size`, and the gate-reach fact, so whoever claims those rows next knows the contract half is done and their plans' contract steps are to be dropped.
